{"obligations":{"reduction":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null},"lower_bound":{"status":"written_but_invalid","quote":"Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component
containing the vertex of \(a_q\).","witness":"COUNTEREXAMPLE: Take q=3 with (a_1,a_2,a_3)=(0.2,0.1,0.7), and make one cut splitting a_3 into 0.36 and 0.34. Then k=1<=q-1 and the sorted pieces are 0.36,0.34,0.20,0.10. The rank pairs create a loop at vertex a_3 and an edge joining a_1 to a_2. Thus the graph has 2<3 edges but contains a loop; moreover, the specifically chosen component containing a_q=a_3 is not a tree and cannot be bipartitioned as claimed.","load_bearing":"The proof of D>=Gamma requires bipartitioning the chosen component so paired pieces contribute signed differences. Since the text has not proved that this component is a tree, the all-cases lower half of the refinement lemma—and hence Liu's matching lower bound—does not follow."},"upper_bound":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null}},"S_valid":1,"wrong_answer_stated":false,"notes":"The drafting reduction and Xiang's construction are valid.
